newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian PM declines comment on minister sex probe.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM declines comment on minister sex probe.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene declined to comment on Thursday on a parliament commission recommendation that Belgium's top court start an investigation into allegations that deputy prime minister Elio Di Rupo had sex with under-age boys.
Asked whether Di Rupo could remain in office and whether Dehaene still backed him, Dehaene's spokeswoman said she could give no comment now.
Dehaene will answer questions in parliament this afternoon, she added. Parliament will meet in full session at 1400 local (1300 GMT) to vote on the commission's recommendation.
A parliament official said it was likely that the vote would be preceded by a debate on the commission's recommendation.

Early on Thursday, after a 16-hour meeting, the 11-member panel decided Di Rupo's constitutional immunity should not be lifted now and that he should not be referred now to the Cour de Cassation -- the country's highest court -- to answer the allegations.

Instead, the commission recommended that the court investigate further the allegations against Di Rupo presented in a report by the Brussels prosecutor-general and recommended the court submit its report to parliament by or before December 9.

Parliament is expected to back the recommendation after the debate and Dehaene's long-awaited appearance after having stayed conspicuously silent about the affair since the allegations against Di Rupo first appeared in a newspaper on Saturday.
The scandal has virtually paralysed the centre-left government. Di Rupo, three other deputy prime ministers and Dehaene form the so-called "core cabinet" which effectively rules Belgium.

Early on Thursday commission member Tony Van Parys, who is a member of Dehaene's christian democrat party CVP, said Di Rupo could remain in function in the coming two and a half weeks of court investigations.
"For me personally I see no reason to tell Di Rupo that he must resign," Van Parys said. The CVP is the largest party in the four-party coalition.
Commission members for the three other coalition parties also said they saw no reason for Di Rupo to resign now.
